correctness.rationale: Lexicographic selected columns t(s)=(s,maximum) give a unit lower-triangular maximal interlacing minor. Weighted deletion equals sum of ordinary partial derivatives on the integral homogeneous polynomial lattice. Integral invertible y_0=x_0, y_i=x_i-x_0 reduces it to partial in y_0, with coefficient j repeated binomial(n-j-1,r-j). Reduction modulo p yields every modular rank. The one-symbol r=n boundary and empty multiset r=1 boundary are explicit. Reconstructed matrices pass 45 parameter tests, 28 exact Smith forms and 180 prime-rank comparisons, not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The naturally occurring semigroup-theoretic weighted and binary interlacing matrices exhibit a sharp integral-versus-modular contrast: every weighted cokernel and p-rank is classified for all natural ranks, while binary interlacing is split surjective over Z. This exact characteristic threshold cannot follow from known balanced margins or real spectrum; it is a structural complete classification, not an arbitrary narrow numerical slice. It does not purport to improve matching existence.
